definitions.explanation: Two children born to the same mother at one birth. A formal, technical word; everyday speech uses {双子|ふたご}.

examples.japanese: {一卵性|いちらんせい}{双生児|そうせいじ}を{研究|けんきゅう}する。
{双生児|そうせいじ}は{遺伝|いでん}の{研究|けんきゅう}でよく{扱|あつか}われる。
examples.english: Twins are often studied in genetic research.

examples.japanese: {一卵性|いちらんせい}{双生児|そうせいじ}と{二卵性|にらんせい}{双生児|そうせいじ}では、{遺伝子|いでんし}の{共通|きょうつう}{度|ど}が{異|こと}なる。
examples.english: Identical twins and fraternal twins differ in how much of their genes they share.

notes:
A formal, scholarly term of Chinese-character origin: {双|そう} (pair) + {生|せい} (birth) + {児|じ} (child). Used in medical, academic, and legal contexts; ordinary conversation uses {双子|ふたご}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一卵性|いちらんせい}{双生児|そうせいじ}: identical (monozygotic) twins
- {二卵性|にらんせい}{双生児|そうせいじ}: fraternal (dizygotic) twins
- {双生児|そうせいじ}{研究|けんきゅう}: twin study

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {双子|ふたご}: twins — the everyday word; {双生児|そうせいじ} is its formal counterpart
- {三|み}つ{子|ご}: triplets — three children born together
